description: The measured feature topology of the Uzbekistan hydrography, declared rather than expanded. Each entry becomes one relationship-table Distribution carrying its predicate, its subject and object types and its measured row count, so the graph knows the links exist and what they mean without holding hundreds of thousands of rows a curator would never review. Ownership follows the subject where the subject is one dataset's features: a reach-to-basin table belongs to the river dataset, not the basin dataset. Where a table's subjects span many datasets, as the atlas overlay does, it belongs to the reference it was measured against.

tables.label: River reach downstream routing
tables.note: Native HydroRIVERS NEXT_DOWN, restricted to reaches inside the selection. target_scope separates a reach that routes to another selected reach from an outlet and from one whose target lies outside Uzbekistan.

tables.label: River reach to level-12 basin
tables.note: The join that makes basins the reference frame. basin_scope records a reach whose basin is outside the published reference rather than dropping the row, which is how 3,073 orphaned reaches went unnoticed before.

tables.label: Water body to level-12 basin
tables.note: Resolved from the lake's pour point, falling back to its centroid. Spatial containment, not a native field of HydroLAKES.

tables.label: Basin downstream routing, levels 01-12
tables.note: Native HydroBASINS routing for every level of the extraction, with the scope of each target recorded against the selection.

tables.label: Basin nesting across levels
tables.note: Child to parent at adjacent levels, matched by Pfafstetter prefix and confirmed by spatial overlap. Every child resolves to exactly one parent.

tables.label: Pfafstetter code nesting
tables.note: The same nesting expressed in Pfafstetter codes rather than basin identifiers. Kept separate because the identifier scheme differs, so the two tables are not directly joinable.

tables.label: Environmental atlas layers by level-12 basin
tables.note: A measured overlay of every atlas package that has published vector geometry onto the basin reference, with overlap area for polygons, length for lines and a feature count for points. This is what lets a basin id reach the atlas: before it, the 134 packages were pinned to the country and nothing finer. Raster packages with only a PNG preview are absent until scripts/raster_to_geojson.py gives them geometry; the manifest names them.

tables.label: Basin downstream routing, lake format, levels 01-12
tables.note: The lake-format counterpart. Lake format splits basins at lakes and therefore mints different HYBAS_IDs, so these rows are not interchangeable with the BasinATLAS ones.

tables.label: Basin nesting across levels, lake format
tables.note: Lake-format child to parent nesting, on lake-format identifiers.

tables.label: Pfafstetter code nesting, lake format
tables.note: Pfafstetter nesting for the lake-format extraction.
